Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Emily and I regrouped and a couple of packaging questions came up as we plan the pilot -> production transition. High level: we want a path that lets us start small, add features per-environment (staging vs prod), and keep upgrade/downgrade friction low. Specific questions:

- Can you describe how "tier banding" works in practice? For example if we start in a smaller band for the pilot and cross the usage threshold mid-term, how does proration work and how immediate is the uplift?
- We have two experimental features (redaction pipeline and private embeddings). Can those be shelved/toggled for pilot and then purchased as add-ons for prod without a full-tier swap?
- If we commit to a 12-month reserved pool for cost predictability, would Redwood support a one-time onboarding credit or a ramped discount structure?

Also, please include any pricing exhibits you typically share for pilot -> reserved conversions and the legal/PO steps you need from procurement. We have a procurement window opening May 18th.

Tracey —

Great questions. Short answers up-front, followed by a recommended path and next steps. I attached our current pricing exhibit (pricing-exhibit-v2.pdf) with band thresholds and add-on SKUs.

Short answers:
- Tier banding/proration: Bands are monthly throughput buckets (example: Band A = up to 10M tokens/mo, Band B = 10–50M, Band C = 50M+). If you exceed a band mid-billing cycle, we bill the overage at the higher band rate for that month and on the following invoice you can elect to move the subscription permanently to the higher band (proration credit applied to unused portion). We can also support automated uplift at a configured threshold if you prefer immediate rebanding.
- Feature shelving/toggles: Yes — redaction pipeline and private embeddings are available as scoped add-ons. They can be enabled per-environment via the Console and charged only when enabled. For pilot we recommend enabling the redaction pipeline in staging and keeping private embeddings off until production (turn-on is immediate, billing begins at next invoice cycle).
- Commitment discounts & onboarding credit: For a 12-month reserved commit we typically offer a one-time onboarding credit (applied to the first invoice) + a stepped discount on committed spend. See Ben's note below with examples.

Recommended path for Acme:
1) Pilot (30–60 days): Band A reserved trial with redaction pipeline enabled in staging (no private embeddings). Keep Band A commit small — this preserves low cost and lets you validate quality.
2) Pre-prod (after pilot): If usage trends to > 40% of Band B capacity for 2 consecutive weeks, we recommend a proactive move to Band B to avoid overage spikes. We can set this to be automated or manual.
3) Prod roll: Upgrade to Band B reserved 12-month commit with private embeddings added as an add-on and a one-time onboarding credit applied.

Operational notes:
- We support scoped feature toggles per project/environment in the Console. They are tied to API keys so you can control prod vs staging access.
- Rollbacks: toggles are immediate and we have guardrails to prevent stateful regressions (KV cache invalidation).

Next steps:
- Ben, can you surface the standard discount matrix and a sample commitment worksheet for Acme?
- Tracey, if that path looks good I can schedule a 30-min handoff with Solutions and Procurement next week (I have Wednesday/Thursday morning slots).

Best,

Looping in pricing details. For Acme's size and pilot trajectory I recommend the following commercial options (examples; final numbers based on measured pilot usage):

Option 1 — 12mo Reserved (recommended)
- 10% recurring discount on committed spend for a 12-month capacity commit (applied to base token/throughput charges)
- One-time onboarding credit equal to one month of Band A reserved spend (applied to first invoice)
- Commitment uplift window: if usage grows into Band B within the first 90 days, we honor proration and do not require additional commit until the 12mo anniversary (helps with growth uncertainty)

Option 2 — Flex / Month-to-Month
- No long-term discount; 5% courtesy discount for customers converting from a Redwood pilot within 30 days of pilot end
- Ability to burst to Dedicated for short-term needs at a premium rate

If Acme prefers a stepped discount (example 5% first 3 months -> 10% thereafter) we can model that in the term sheet; attached is a simple worksheet that you can use to estimate spend and the effective discount (discount-term-sheet.xlsx).

If Procurement is comfortable, we can apply Option 1 with the onboarding credit and I will prepare a draft commercial exhibit and DocuSign packet for signature.

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs before I share with procurement: 

1) Proration detail: if we elect to move permanently from Band A to Band B mid-billing-cycle, how is the unused portion of the Band A commit credited? Is that an invoice-level credit or is it applied as a balance?
2) Feature toggles: can we restrict an add-on (private embeddings) to specific API keys so only prod traffic is billed? Want to make sure we don't accidentally incur charges from staging tests.
3) Trial extension: can Redwood extend our existing pilot credits by 30 days if we sign a letter of intent (LOI) for a reserved 12-month commit? Procurement prefers LOIs before drafting PO windows.

If you can confirm those three points I will push this to Procurement next Monday.

—Tracey
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-02T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tier banding and feature shelfing — Acme pilot to prod

Tracey —

Answers inline: 
1) Proration: unused portion of the Band A commit is issued as an invoice credit applied to the next invoice (not an account-level cash refund). We also show proforma credits in the Console so Procurement can see net-first-invoice impact.
2) Feature toggles/API keys: yes, add-ons can be scoped to API keys and to Console projects. You can restrict private embeddings to your prod API key(s) so staging calls are blocked or routed to the non-private embeddings SKU.
3) Trial extension: we can offer a 30-day extension on pilot credits if Acme signs an LOI expressing intent to move to a 12-month reserved commit within 30 days of pilot end. I'll prepare a short LOI template and Ben will include the commercial exhibit in the DocuSign packet.

Ben — approved to proceed with Option 1 (10% 12mo + onboarding credit) for Acme, subject to pilot usage validation and legal standard terms. Lukas — please schedule the 30-min handoff with Tracey for next Wed/Thu as proposed; I'll review the LOI once drafted.
